text:
All tests pass. The fix:

- **Before:** `line.split("=")` split on every `=`, so `parts[1]` was only the text between the first and second `=` (truncating `?debug=1`), and `parts[1].split("#")[0]` cut values at the first `#` (emptying `#ff8800`).
- **After:** `line.split("=", 1)` splits only at the first `=`, and the value is taken as everything after it, stripped of surrounding whitespace — matching the documented behavior (values may contain `=`, `#`, `;`; no inline comments).

arguments.summary: Fixed inifile/parser.py: replaced `line.split("=")` + `parts[1].split("#")[0]` with `line.split("=", 1)` and using the full remainder as the value (stripped). This stops truncating values at a second `=` (e.g. `http://localhost:8000/?debug=1`) or at `#` (e.g. `#ff8800`), while preserving the documen...
